reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an ASMR-style performance with a tech-support theme, and the depicted software installation, remote access, ransom demands, and threats are not established as a real support interaction or computer compromise. The visible Subscribe graphic requests ordinary audience engagement without making payment, data disclosure, software installation, or computer access a condition.

citations.quote: ASMR Indian Microsoft Tech Support
I am calling from Microsoft tech support there seems to be a problem with your computer
I need to put a certain number so I can have access to your computer I will take over your computer to fix the problem for you.
You must give me $500 or I will delete every file

opening.argument: The video presents a concrete payment-for-access relationship, not merely a general technology discussion. The speaker claims Microsoft support, directs the target to an external website and software download, and asks for a number to take control of the computer. After that access is claimed, payment is explicitly tied to restoring control: the demand is $500, later escalates to one million rupees, and release is promised only after payment. That is a direct solicitation involving an asset and a required viewer action.

citations.quote: I am calling from Microsoft tech support there seems to be a problem with your computer
This will take you to a software download page Download the software please
I need to put a certain number so I can have access to your computer I will take over your computer to fix the problem for you.
Once I have received the payment I will free your computer from my hands and you will have it in your hands

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the presentation ASMR does not remove the operational sequence it depicts: an asserted support identity, software download, remote access, and a payment demand linked to release. The title establishes a format, but does not disprove that the dialogue is a solicitation. Likewise, a Subscribe graphic addresses the channel, while the spoken demand addresses payment for the computer.

citations.quote: ASMR Indian Microsoft Tech Support
You must give me $500 or I will delete every file
Once I have received the payment I will free your computer from my hands and you will have it in your hands

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited words show only what the performance says, not that a real computer was accessed, held, or offered back. The title identifies the content as ASMR tech-support entertainment, and the supplied frame shows a person performing into a microphone. Nothing establishes that viewers were actually asked to transfer money or that the described sequence occurred outside the performance.

citations.quote: ASMR Indian Microsoft Tech Support
I need to put a certain number so I can have access to your computer I will take over your computer to fix the problem for you.

opening.argument: The combination of signals is unusually coercive and unsafe: an alleged Microsoft representative identifies a computer problem, sends the target to an external website, requests a software download, seeks a number for remote control, and then demands money. The demand is accompanied by file-deletion threats, a payment address, escalating amounts, and a five-day deadline. Even if the video uses exaggerated delivery, these are the same concrete mechanics a viewer would need to recognize as a scam: authority, access, urgency, and payment pressure in one sequence.

citations.quote: Then you will click on first button that appears on website It is very simple process
Download the software please It is not virus. it is good for your computer
You must give me $500 or I will delete every file
You have five days. Five. I have your computer, beta

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each warning sign as harmless because the presenter is visible, but visibility does not neutralize the combination of external download, remote-control request, payment address, threats, and deadline. The absence of proof of an actual compromise is not proof that the depicted solicitation lacks scam characteristics. The dialogue itself supplies the risk pattern the audience is being shown.

citations.quote: my paypal is paljit singh at yahoo.com Simply send the money to this account 500
You have five days. Five. I have your computer, beta
Download the software please It is not virus. it is good for your computer

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The red flags are delivered as an exaggerated script, and the evidence does not show that any download, remote access, payment, threat, or deadline was real. The frame shows a performer at a microphone, while the title explicitly calls the work ASMR tech-support content. A fictional depiction can contain scam-like mechanics without itself soliciting a real transaction.

citations.quote: ASMR Indian Microsoft Tech Support
But but I have your computer for ransom Aaaaah, I have your computer now

opening.argument: The entertainment wrapper can function as a vehicle for promotion rather than a safeguard against it. The title adopts the recognizable Microsoft tech-support role, while the spoken performance gives viewers a complete participation pathway: visit an external site, download software, provide a number for access, and send payment to an identified account. The channel description also solicits audience engagement through a subscription appeal. A light ASMR presentation therefore packages a concrete access-and-payment scenario in a form designed to hold attention and encourage response.

citations.quote: ASMR Indian Microsoft Tech Support
Then you will click on first button that appears on website It is very simple process This will take you to a software download page Download the software please
my paypal is paljit singh at yahoo.com Simply send the money to this account 500
Show your support by liking the video and subscribing if you want to see more awesome videos.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense assumes that a performance label settles the meaning of the content, but the role adopted is precisely what gives the instructions their apparent authority. The title does not negate the repeated directions to use a website, download software, grant access, and pay. Ordinary channel promotion also does not explain away the separate payment account and ransom language.

citations.quote: ASMR Indian Microsoft Tech Support
This will take you to a software download page Download the software please
my paypal is paljit singh at yahoo.com Simply send the money to this account 500

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The performance framing is not incidental: the title calls it ASMR, the supplied visual shows the presenter speaking into a microphone, and the description asks viewers to like and subscribe to the channel. Those contextual signals support entertainment rather than a real promotion of remote-access services. The dialogue provides no evidence that anyone was directed to complete the scenario in reality.
